cognate: Ved. jāgṛ- (jāgrat-, jāgṛvi-, pf. jāgāra) = Av. jaγāurvah-, jaγāra = Gk ἐγρήγορα, ἐγρηγορώς: the reduplicated stem *h₁ge-h₁gor- of *h₁ger- 'be awake' (Gk ἐγείρω is the simplex). Ved. svap-, svápna-, a-svapna- = Av. xᵛafsa-, a-xᵛafniia-, an-ava-xᵛabdəmna- = Gk ὕπνος, ἄ-υπνος (*swep-, *swep-no-, *n̥-swep-no-).
drift_or_renewal: Greek renews the finite and participial 'sleep' member with εὕδω/καθεύδω (Symp. 203a, Leges 824a, Heraclitus) but keeps *swep- in the noun ὕπνος (Resp. 476c ἐν ὕπνῳ ... ἐγρηγορώς) and in the privative ἄυπνος (Ti. 52b). The 'wake' member stays cognate throughout. In the guardian use Greek renews 'protect' (φρουρέω, φυλάσσω, σῴζω) where Indo-Iranian keeps *peh₂- (Ved. pāyú-, pāntu; Av. nipāiti).
shared_syntax: A polar pair of the two states. Either coordinated participles or conditionals, 'waking or sleeping' (Ved. jāgrato yat svapantaḥ, yadi jāgrad yadi svapan, suptān jāgrato vā; Gk ἐγρηγορόσι καὶ καθεύδουσι, ἐάν τε ἐν ὕπνῳ ἐάν τ’ ἐγρηγορώς), or a coordinated epithet pair 'sleepless and wakeful' (Ved. asvapno yaś ca jāgṛviḥ; Av. axᵛafniiąm ... jaγāurum; Gk ἄυπνον ... ἐγερθέντες).
context: The anchors share a dream setting. RV 10.164 and AVŚ 6.45 are charms against evil dreams, removing the misdeeds 'we committed waking or sleeping'. Plato Ti. 52b contrasts our dreamlike state with the 'sleepless, truly existing nature' that we cannot state correctly 'when awakened'; Resp. 476c defines dreaming 'whether in sleep or awake' in the same terms. Outside the slab, Indo-Iranian uses the pair as an epithet of vigilant guardians: the Adityas and Agni's spies are ásvapnajaḥ ... pāyávaḥ; sleepless gods guard the earth (AVŚ 12.1.7); Av. Sraoša and Mithra 'unsleeping, with watchfulness, protect'; Yt 19.38 and Y 62.5 have 'upright-legged, sleepless, wakeful'. Greek also uses ἄυπνος and ἐγρηγορός of guardians: Aesch. PV 31-32 'you will guard the rock, standing upright, sleepless'; Eum. 705-6 'a wakeful guard of the land on behalf of the sleepers'; Argus; the fleece-dragon. A further possible link is the cluster 'upright + sleepless/awake' (Av. ərəδβō.zəṇga- + axᵛafniia-; Gk ὀρθοστάδην ἄυπνος; Ved. ūrdhvaḥ supteṣu jāgāra), with *h₃r̥dʰwó- (ərəδβa-, ὀρθός, ūrdhvá-) cognate in all three.
phrase: *h₁ge-h₁gor- ~ *swep-: 'waking or sleeping' / 'sleepless and wakeful' (Ved. jāgrato yat svapantaḥ, asvapno jāgṛviḥ; Av. axᵛafniia- jaγāurvah-; Gk ἄυπνος ... ἐγερθέντες, ἐγρηγορόσι καὶ καθεύδουσι)
note: Caveat: 'waking or sleeping' is a natural polar expression, and these are the default words in each language, so the merism by itself could arise independently. Three things argue for inheritance. The same reduplicated perfect/intensive stem, not the simplex, carries the 'wake' member in all three branches. Indo-Iranian has the exact coordinated epithet pair (asvapna- + jāgṛvi- = axᵛafniia- + jaγāurvah-). Both Indo-Iranian and Greek attach the pair to vigilant guardian figures. Recalled: the comparison of sleepless, wakeful Mithra (Yt 10.7 aβaxᵛafnəm jaγāurvåŋhəm) with Vedic ásvapnaj- epithets. The Greek parallels and the dream-context congruence come from the passages and the searches.

cognate: Gk δεξιός = Lat. dexter (*deḱs-i-/-tero-); Gk λαιός = Lat. laeuus (*leh₂i-wo-; cf. OCS lěvъ)
drift_or_renewal: Greek prose and Homer renew 'left' with ἀριστερός: in GLAUx to 250 BC, 238 sentences pair δεξιός with ἀριστερός against 6 with λαιός; Homer has 3 with ἀριστερός and none with λαιός. Latin has sinister beside laeuus, but the LASLA sample has no dexter+sinister sentence against 4 with laeuus.
shared_syntax: A coordinated antonym pair 'right and left' (asyndetic, with τε/que, or εἴτε ... εἴτε), used as a spatial merism 'on both sides / all over': both ship walls (Eur. Hel. 1573), either wing (Rhes. 485), 'right with left' in the transposition of parts (Lucr. 2.488, 4.430).
context: Battle lines and ship sides in Euripides; mirror inversion and transposition of parts in Lucretius. The only congruence is the pairing itself.
note: Weak evidence: coordinating two antonyms is close to inevitable once both words exist. Reported only because in both languages the old *laiwo- word (poetic λαιός, Latin laeuus) appears in the pair beside a commoner rival, which may preserve an inherited pairing. Not claimed as a poetic formula.

Nearly all pivots are Plato prose (Leges, Timaeus, Critias). The partners were matched by shared roots and are mostly Cato's De agricultura, Lucretius and the AV, sharing only common numerals and kinship words. Rejected leads: Plato Ti. 76d bone + sinew 'mixed' ~ Lucr. 1.866, because Lucretius is rendering Anaxagorean doctrine from Greek and the AV and Hippocratic body-part lists are generic anatomy; mother/father/son lists and ordinal series; the AVŚ 4.12 'joint to joint' healing charm, which has no congruent partner in the slab.
